answer_key.intent: A degrading disk/slow follower on kafka-1 causes slow log flushes, replicas dropping out of ISR, slower produce requests and growing consumer lag.
An analyst runs a huge unbounded ad-hoc cross join off-hours that saturates both Trino workers; other queries queue and some fail.

A state/heap leak in a Flink taskmanager (unbounded keyed state in the enrichment join) drives heap up and GC thrash, causing backpressure, slow checkpoints and eventually checkpoint timeouts and reduced throughput.
Someone pauses the customer_agg DAG during maintenance and forgets it; scheduled Spark runs do not happen and the executors stay idle.
A client with huge fetch batches fills kafka-2's heap: long GC pauses, slower produce, and repeated ISR drops.
Airflow scheduler degrades from a bloated metadata DB / DAG-parse storm: loop saturates CPU, heartbeat goes stale, tasks pile up in queued state.
A new orders-etl-consumer release is slower per record than the produce rate; lag builds until rollback, then drains.

A Spark Structured Streaming executor (orders-stream-exec-2) slowly leaks memory (unbounded state/broadcast cache); heap and GC climb, batches slow, scheduling delay builds, and the pod nears its memory limit and gets OOMKilled.
A bad config rollout makes orders-producer crash on startup; it loops in restarts and no orders arrive until fixed.
A Flink job update keeps keyed state forever, so both TaskManagers' memory creeps up slowly over hours.
A runaway ad-hoc cross-join query lands on trino-worker-0, eating heap and CPU; GC thrashes, other queries slow and queue in the adhoc resource group, and some fail on memory limits.
